spec: Compute factorial(10) recursively and print the result on its own line.
Compute the 25th Fibonacci number iteratively (F(1)=1, F(2)=1) and print it on its own line.
For each of the integers 1, 2, 13, 15, 97 in that order, print 1 if it is prime else 0, one per line.
Print the sum of the decimal digits of 987654321 on its own line.
Reverse the decimal digits of 12345 and print the result on its own line.
Compute 2^10 iteratively (integer exponentiation, no library) and print it on its own line.
aic:
[: main [] [D
  [! result 1]
  [! i 0]
  [W [< i 10] [D
    [! result [* result 2]]
    [! i [+ i 1]]
  ]]
  [. [N result]]
]]
[main]

spec: Define a 4-field record (x, y, w, h). For a rectangle with x=2, y=5, w=10, h=4, print the area on the first line and the perimeter on the second line.
aic:
[:: Rect x y w h]

[: main [] [D
  [! r [Rect 2 5 10 4]]
  [! x [@@.Rect:x r]]
  [! y [@@.Rect:y r]]
  [! w [@@.Rect:w r]]
  [! h [@@.Rect:h r]]
  [! area [* w h]]
  [! perim [* 2 [+ w h]]]
  [. [N area]]
  [. [N perim]]
]]

[main]

spec: Define a record with fields (value, next) where next is a pointer to the same record type. Build a 5-node chain manually with values 10,20,30,40,50 (node i points to node i+1; the last's next is 0). Traverse from the head and print the sum of the value fields on its own line.
aic:
[:: Node value next]

[: main [] [D
  [! n5 [Node 50 0]]
  [! n4 [Node 40 n5]]
  [! n3 [Node 30 n4]]
  [! n2 [Node 20 n3]]
  [! n1 [Node 10 n2]]
  [! sum 0]
  [! cur n1]
  [W [!= cur 0]
    [! sum [+ sum [@@.Node:value cur]]]
    [! cur [@@$.Node:next cur]]
  ]
  [. [N sum]]
]]

[main]

spec: Define a 3-field record (a, b, c). Use the bulk field setter to set all fields in a single call to 11, 22, 33. Then read each field back individually and print them on one line separated by single spaces, then a newline.
aic:
[import "lib/string.aic"]

[:: Rec a b c]

[: main [] [D
  [! r [Rec 0 0 0]]
  [@@!.Rec r 11 22 33]
  [! a [@@.Rec:a r]]
  [! b [@@.Rec:b r]]
  [! c [@@.Rec:c r]]
  [! sa [str_from_int a]]
  [! sb [str_from_int b]]
  [! sc [str_from_int c]]
  [! t1 [str_cat sa " "]]
  [! t2 [str_cat t1 sb]]
  [! t3 [str_cat t2 " "]]
  [! line [str_cat t3 sc]]
  [. line]
]]

[main]

spec: Allocate a word buffer. Store the 10 fixed integers 1..10 via word operations. Then iterate and read them back with word operations, and print their sum on its own line.
aic:
[import "lib/string.aic"]

[: main [] [D
  [! buf [H 80]]
  [@> 10 [i] [D
    [@@! buf i [+ i 1]]
  ]]
  [! sum 0]
  [@> 10 [i] [D
    [! v [@@ buf i]]
    [! sum [+ sum v]]
  ]]
  [. [N sum]]
]]

[main]

spec: Define a 1-field record (radius). For radii 2, 3, and 5, compute the area as radius*radius*3 (integer approximation, no float) and print each area on its own line, in that order.
aic:
[:: Circle radius]

[: main [] [D
  [! r1 [Circle 2]]
  [! r2 [Circle 3]]
  [! r3 [Circle 5]]
  [! x1 [@@.Circle:radius r1]]
  [! x2 [@@.Circle:radius r2]]
  [! x3 [@@.Circle:radius r3]]
  [! a1 [* [* x1 x1] 3]]
  [! a2 [* [* x2 x2] 3]]
  [! a3 [* [* x3 x3] 3]]
  [! s1 [N a1]]
  [! s2 [N a2]]
  [! s3 [N a3]]
  [. s1]
  [. s2]
  [. s3]
]]

[main]

spec: Using lib/vec.aic, push the 10 integers 1..10 onto a vector. Then pop them off one at a time and print the sum of all popped values on its own line.
aic:
[import "lib/vec.aic"]

[: main [] [D
  [! v [vec_new 10]]
  [@> 10 [i] [D
    [! x [+ i 1]]
    [vec_push v x]
  ]]
  [! sum 0]
  [W [> [vec_len v] 0] [D
    [! x [vec_pop v]]
    [! sum [+ sum x]]
  ]]
  [! out [N sum]]
  [. out]
]]

[main]

spec: Using lib/map.aic, insert the 5 key->int pairs a=10, b=20, c=30, d=40, e=50 into a map. Then look up each key in the order a, b, c, d, e and print each value on its own line, in that order.
aic:
[import "lib/map.aic"]
[import "lib/string.aic"]

[: main [] [D
  [! m [map_new 8]]
  [! ka [H 1]]
  [@! ka 0 97]
  [! kb [H 1]]
  [@! kb 0 98]
  [! kc [H 1]]
  [@! kc 0 99]
  [! kd [H 1]]
  [@! kd 0 100]
  [! ke [H 1]]
  [@! ke 0 101]
  [map_set m ka 10]
  [map_set m kb 20]
  [map_set m kc 30]
  [map_set m kd 40]
  [map_set m ke 50]
  [! v1 [map_get m ka]]
  [! v2 [map_get m kb]]
  [! v3 [map_get m kc]]
  [! v4 [map_get m kd]]
  [! v5 [map_get m ke]]
  [. [N v1]]
  [. [N v2]]
  [. [N v3]]
  [. [N v4]]
  [. [N v5]]
]]

[main]

spec: Using lib/map.aic, insert the 5 key->int pairs a=10, b=20, c=30, d=40, e=50 into a map. Then for each key in the order a, b, c, d, e report whether the map contains it (1 if present, 0 if not) using the membership/contains accessor, printing each on its own line, in that order.
aic:
[import "lib/map.aic"]
[import "lib/string.aic"]

[: main []
  [D
    [! m [map_new 8]]
    [map_set m "a" 10]
    [map_set m "b" 20]
    [map_set m "c" 30]
    [map_set m "d" 40]
    [map_set m "e" 50]
    [! k1 "a"]
    [! k2 "b"]
    [! k3 "c"]
    [! k4 "d"]
    [! k5 "e"]
    [! c1 [map_contains m k1]]
    [! c2 [map_contains m k2]]
    [! c3 [map_contains m k3]]
    [! c4 [map_contains m k4]]
    [! c5 [map_contains m k5]]
    [. [N c1]]
    [. [N c2]]
    [. [N c3]]
    [. [N c4]]
    [. [N c5]]
  ]
]

[main]

spec: Using lib/json.aic, build a JSON object with a string field "greeting"="hi", an int field "n"=42, and a nested array field "list"=[1,2,3]. Stringify it, then parse the stringified result back. Print, each on its own line in this order: the recovered string field value, the recovered int field value, and the recovered array length.
aic:
[import "lib/json.aic"]

[: main [] [D
  [! o [json_obj]]
  [! g [json_str "hi"]]
  [! nv [json_int 42]]
  [! arr [json_arr]]
  [! one [json_int 1]]
  [! two [json_int 2]]
  [! three [json_int 3]]
  [json_arr_push arr one]
  [json_arr_push arr two]
  [json_arr_push arr three]
  [json_obj_set o "greeting" g]
  [json_obj_set o "n" nv]
  [json_obj_set o "list" arr]
  [! s [json_stringify o]]
  [! p [json_parse s]]
  [! rg [json_obj_get p "greeting"]]
  [! rn [json_obj_get p "n"]]
  [! ra [json_obj_get p "list"]]
  [! gs [json_get_str rg]]
  [! ni [json_get_int rn]]
  [! al [json_arr_len ra]]
  [! gs2 [json_get_str rg]]
  [! ns [N ni]]
  [! als [N al]]
  [. gs2]
  [. ns]
  [. als]
]]

[main]

spec: Using lib/arena.aic, create an arena. Allocate 3 chunks (4 bytes, 8 bytes, 16 bytes). Record the arena offset after the 3 allocations. Then reset the arena and print, on its own line, the arena offset after the reset (which must be 0).
aic:
[import "lib/arena.aic"]

[: main []
  [D
    [! a [arena_new 256]]
    [! c1 [arena_alloc a 4]]
    [! c2 [arena_alloc a 8]]
    [! c3 [arena_alloc a 16]]
    [! off1 [arena_offset a]]
    [arena_reset a]
    [! off2 [arena_offset a]]
    [! s [N off2]]
    [. s]
  ]
]

[main]

spec: Using lib/string.aic, given the string "benchmark_suite", print whether it starts with the prefix "bench" and whether it ends with the suffix "_suite" (two numbers, 1 for yes / 0 for no) space-separated on one line, then a newline.
aic:
[import "lib/string.aic"]

[: main [] [D
  [! s "benchmark_suite"]
  [! sp "bench"]
  [! sf "_suite"]
  [! a [str_starts_with s sp]]
  [! b [str_ends_with s sf]]
  [! na [N a]]
  [! nb [N b]]
  [! out [str_cat [str_cat na " "] nb]]
  [. out]
]]

[main]

spec: Using lib/map.aic, given the list of 8 strings: ant, bee, bee, cat, cat, dog, dog, ant. Count the frequency of each distinct string using a map. Then print each distinct string (in the fixed order ant, bee, cat, dog) followed by a single space and its count, one per line.
aic:
[import "lib/map.aic"]
[import "lib/string.aic"]

[: main [] [D
  [! m [map_new 8]]
  [! words [vec_new 8]]
  [vec_push words "ant"]
  [vec_push words "bee"]
  [vec_push words "bee"]
  [vec_push words "cat"]
  [vec_push words "cat"]
  [vec_push words "dog"]
  [vec_push words "dog"]
  [vec_push words "ant"]
  [! n [vec_len words]]
  [@> n [i] [D
    [! w [vec_get words i]]
    [! c [map_get m w]]
    [! nc [+ c 1]]
    [map_set m w nc]
  ]]
  [! keys [vec_new 4]]
  [vec_push keys "ant"]
  [vec_push keys "bee"]
  [vec_push keys "cat"]
  [vec_push keys "dog"]
  [! kn [vec_len keys]]
  [@> kn [j] [D
    [! k [vec_get keys j]]
    [! c [map_get m k]]
    [! cs [N c]]
    [! line [str_cat k " "]]
    [. [str_cat line cs]]
  ]]
]]
[main]

spec: Using lib/io.aic, write the fixed string 'Hello AIC benchmark input line' (30 characters, no trailing newline) to a file named bench_in.txt. Then read that file back and print 1 on its own line if the recovered content exactly matches the original AND the reported file size equals the string length (30), else 0.
aic:
[import "lib/io.aic"]
[import "lib/string.aic"]

[: main [] [D
  [! content "Hello AIC benchmark input line"]
  [! len [L content]]
  [! w [io_write_file "bench_in.txt" content]]
  [! sz [io_file_size "bench_in.txt"]]
  [! back [io_read_file "bench_in.txt"]]
  [! eq [str_eq back content]]
  [! ok [&& [== eq 1] [== sz len]]]
  [. [N ok]]
]]

[main]
